_help.about: A boss in every dungeon (Mike, 6 Oct, 21:20): one unique, creepy mythical creature per pocket world's dungeon (§EW). It prowls only the dark: the rooms and corridors not yet relit. Every relight shrinks its ground; the last light drives it back into its lair, a hole in a cave somewhere in the dungeon. Not a fight: no health bar, nothing to kill (§ET.1). The creatures are Mike's; moves, tells and numbers are Claude (chat)'s first guesses, 6 Oct; the designer owns them. Wired 7 Oct (Claude Code, queue 49, §EY.8 step 1; Boss, BossGround, BossBody, BossSounds in scripts/crawler/): rule, contact, lair, release and bosses.desert, the snake, which stands in the tomb as the test while the tomb's world is open (the boss marked first). The other bosses are NOT WIRED YET: each comes with its world (§EY.8 step 2). The snake strikes through queue 57's CreatureStrike (its strike block; the torch's stagger works on its wind-up) and holds queue 56's Pursuit while it hunts you (its gives_up block; you don't heal while it has you). Since Mike's note of 7 Oct (Claude Code): nothing physical goes through the stone or appears anywhere; the snake moves only at its speeds, frame by frame, crossing lit rooms on the dimmest way (crawler.json light_field) or under them through its own tunnels (bosses.desert.tunnels), and a chase stops at the edge of the light (residents.json rules.chase_light_cap).
_help.rule: §EY.1 (Mike). one_per_dungeon. ground: unlit, the rooms and corridors not yet relit (crawler.json holders; §EX.4: one hearth per dungeon, torches in every other room). A room counts as relit once every torch in it is lit; a corridor stretch between two lit sconces counts as lit; the hearth room is never its ground (Claude). never_blocks_exit: §EX.5 holds, it is a danger, never a gate. relit_closes_room: a relit room is closed to it for good (§ET.4, relit stays lit). puts_out_relit: never. leaves_lit_room: if you relight the room it is in, it leaves for the nearest dark (Claude). torch_in_hand: delay, relit_room: safe (§BA's rule made the boss's). last_light: to_lair. notice: how far it sees a carried flame and hears a sprint (Claude's first guess). chase_enters_light (§FD, Mike): a boss that has hit you can follow you into the light; a relit room stays closed to its prowling, not to a chase in progress. Amended by Mike's note of 7 Oct (§FD; Claude Code): a chase, its strike landed or not, comes toward the light only as far as its edge (residents.json rules.chase_light_cap, on crawler.json light_field: never close to a fire), rearing its head into the glow (bosses.<world>.peek_m); it strikes you only within its reach of where it may stand, so by the hearth or a relit torch you are safe and at the light's dim edge you are not; once it gives you up it is back in the dark within residents.json rules.back_to_dark_s. Its prowling still never enters a lit room or stretch. (Queue 56 had let a chase that had hit you follow you into any lit room but the hearth room.) Built for the snake (queue 49; Boss, BossGround): a room is one node and a corridor or stair is cut at each sconce into stretches; a stretch is lit when every end of it is (a lit sconce, or a door into a lit node; an end with nothing there, a dead end or the way out, never darkens it), and a room with no torch of its own takes the light round it, so the ground reaches nothing exactly at the last holder. It moves only through dark nodes and never through the hearth room; if the node it is in is lit round it, it leaves at once for the nearest dark by the way with least light in it, under the light through its own tunnels where they lead there (bosses.<world>.tunnels), else across the lit rooms on the dimmest way (crawler.json light_field), the hearth room only when there is no other way: since Mike's note of 7 Oct it never goes into the stone nor comes up elsewhere (queue 49 had it go below, out of your sight, when cut off). notice: your lit torch in its line of sight within sees_flame_m, you sprinting within hears_sprint_m, or (bosses.<world>.feels_m) you close enough to touch whatever your light. relit_room safe: by the fire you are out of its reach (the chase's edge, above).
_help.contact: §EY.2 (Claude's first guess, open for Mike, §EY.7 call 2). A strike is one hit in harm.json (§EA, §EC): three and it's 'Good night'. You wake at the hearth (§ET.3) and every light you relit is still lit. Built: its strike lands through CreatureStrike, the player's take_hit, so harm.json's invuln_s holds between hits; the third plays 'Good night' (Harm), then you wake on the mat by the hearth (CrawlerMain) with your torches in your pack (the lit one went out as you fell), every relit holder still lit, and the boss lets you go where it is and goes on with its rounds from there (Mike's note of 7 Oct: nothing appears anywhere it didn't travel to; queue 49 had it back at the far end of its dark).
_help.lair: §EY.1 (Mike): usually a hole in a cave somewhere in the dungeon. off_main_path, findable (Claude). breathing_heard_m: once it is driven in you can stand at the edge and hear it below. enterable: false is Claude's first guess (§EY.7 call 3). Built (BossGround.place_lair, TombBuild._lair_hole, Boss): the tomb has no caves, so the hole is the floor of a side room off the main way (a dead end where there is one) broken through into the dark below, placed clear of its doors, fires, airways, the line between its doors and what stands on its floor (in a crypt, where one of its coffins stood, fallen through: never a skeleton's grave nor beside an open one's lid): a black mouth hole_r_m across (Claude Code, 7 Oct), flags tipped into it, broken stone and small bones round it. A ring of collision keeps you at the edge (enterable false). The breathing plays from below the floor there once the boss is home. Since §EX.1/§EX.3 (queue 48, Claude Code, 7 Oct) its broken stone is the tomb's style stone, and it keeps clear of the pillars its room will stand on (its rim at least BossGround.PILLAR_KEEP_M, 1.35 m, from a pillar's middle: room to walk between; in a crypt, a coffin a pillar stands on is never laid, so never taken). Since Mike's note of 7 Oct (Claude Code) its hole is where it goes physically: a fire pot's burst stuns it (bosses.<world>.stun_s), it flees to the hole (through its tunnels or on the dimmest way) and down it, out of the pots' reach, for fire_pots.json vs_boss.drives_off_s, then comes up out of it onto its rounds; at the last light it goes down it for good (release). Mike: 'you might be able to go down a lair later'; not yet (enterable false).
_help.release: §EY.2 (Claude's first guess). When the last light catches you hear it go: a long sound travelling away and down to its hole, then the dungeon's small sounds come back (bed_returns). log_line: the one log entry (no bestiary, §BA: nothing names it on screen). Built (Boss.release; since Mike's note of 7 Oct it never vanishes): wherever it is when the last light catches, it flees to its lair physically, through its tunnels or across the lit tomb on the dimmest way, at bosses.<world>.flee_mps, and goes down its hole for good; the long cry goes with it (cry_s); the tomb's small sounds (the drips) are hushed by bed_hush_db while it prowls and come back over bed_return_s once it is home (Claude Code's numbers, 7 Oct). The log line gets a full stop.
_help.bosses: §EY.3. Keyed by worlds.json worlds. creature: Mike's words. world_by: who placed it in that world (Mike, or Claude's pick, open). pattern: how it moves (each its own; Mike: 'a different algorithm'). Speeds are m/s; the ambient walk is 4.3 and the sprint 5.6 (movement.json profiles.ambient), and a sprint held too long gutters the torch (§ET.7). tell: what you hear or see before it. first: the one to build first (the tomb's). §FE.4 (6 Oct, 22:32): the swamp's boss is the witch (Mike) and the mine's the giant spider (Claude's reading, open); the hornet and the centipede moved to unplaced. §FJ.6 (Mike, 22:52): the centipede is the jungle's boss (the jungle isn't in worlds.json yet, §EW.2). Built: desert only (the snake). Its extra numbers (hunt_mps, leave_mps, torch_delay, feels_m, watch_s, body) are Claude Code's first guesses, 7 Oct; desert._help says what each does.
_help.gives_up: §FD (Claude Code's first guess, 7 Oct, queue 56; Mike tunes it): how a boss gives up a chase, its own mix of residents.json rules.gives_up, read by Pursuit (scripts/crawler/pursuit.gd). distance_m: you got farther from it than this (the snake's is past its sight of a flame, rule.notice.sees_flame_m 20). out_of_sight_s: it hasn't seen your flame or heard you run for this long. hide: true, crouched out of its sight behind cover you are as lost to it as anywhere out of sight (§FC.2). torch_doused: true, it hunts your flame, so your torch going out while it chases you loses you at once. Until it gives you up you don't heal (harm.json fd.recover_starts), a chase comes only as far as the light's edge (residents.json rules.chase_light_cap, Mike's note of 7 Oct); after giving up it is back in the dark within residents.json rules.back_to_dark_s.
_help.unplaced: §FE.4: bosses with no world yet: the centipede and the hornet (moved out of the mine and the swamp), the imps (Mike, 22:39) and the warden (Mike, 22:40). chain: null until Mike answers §FI.2 call 6 (§EH: no metal; a found relic, bone or wood links, or rope; §EH is superseded by §FL.1, 7 Oct: metal is back, so a forged chain fits, §FL.1 call 1). one_or_pack: null until Mike says. §FJ.6: the centipede moved to bosses.jungle; the imps go to another world, not chosen yet.
_help.strike: §FA.1, §FA.2 (prompt 57; wired by Claude Code in the crawler, CreatureStrike). A boss strikes as a resident does: a wind-up of wind_up_s with its own tell, seen and heard (tell: the words; sound: its SoundSynth voice, played from the creature from the wind-up's first frame; its sprite's pose), then the committed strike, strike_s, which lands one hit (contact) if you are still within reach_m of where its body struck from (CreatureStrike.origin: the snake's lies where it rears, not its head as it lunges out) with nothing solid between, then recover_s before the next. A swing of a lit torch that reaches it during the wind-up (body_r: how big a target its head is) staggers it (torch.json stagger: reel_s, cooldown_s, no damage) and it reels back reel_m. Left out: strike_s 0.2, recover_s 0.8, reel_m 1.0, body_r 0.4 (CreatureStrike.DEFAULTS). bosses.desert.strike, the snake's: Claude's first guesses, 6 Oct night (the tell is Claude (chat)'s, §FA.2); reach_m is §EY's strike_m; the hiss and the head drawn back for 0.7 s, then a 0.15 s lunge.
_help.pharaoh: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FO.1] The Egyptian ruin's boss (Mike, 10 Oct): a mummy pharaoh, a 'King Tut sarcophagus type' that opens up, never killable. In 'unplaced' because no biome world holds the Egyptian ruin yet (§FO.9 call 2; bosses.<world> is keyed by worlds.json). Its lair is its own sarcophagus: the lid grinds aside while it prowls and grinds shut when the last light drives it in (the §EY.2 release, styled as a sarcophagus instead of a hole; not enterable, like the hole). Its behaviours are not talked through, so it has no pattern, no numbers and no strike block (a strike block would join stagger_check's count and its tell must differ from the mummy resident's), and no entry in boss_pool.json (pools.size() is checked against bosses, not unplaced). Phase two (ruin_loop.json) applies to it as to every boss. Queue 89 builds it.

mine.tell: silk ticking on stone, then silence
mine.mike: in a mine shaft, an abandoned mine shaft, there'd be a giant spider … webs hanging around … creep throughout the walls and ceiling and even on the floor, similar to the centipede

mountains.tell: a howl when it picks you up
mountains.mike: a wolfman type boss that lives in a cave-style ruin

swamp.tell: her voice, sweet, calling you in
swamp.mike: a creepy witch lady that roams the halls and tries to get you to make her stew

strike.tell: a hiss and the head drawing back

desert.mike: a giant snake which slithers through the halls
desert._help: Claude Code's first guesses (7 Oct, queue 49; Mike tunes by playing). speed_mps: its rounds, slow and steady. hunt_mps: hunting you; 4.6 since Mike's note of 7 Oct ('the snake should be faster or just as fast as a walk and if you sprint you can outrun it'): faster than your walk (4.3), slower than your sprint (5.6), so walking it catches you and sprinting you get away; it keeps coming through its wind-up and its lunge at up to hunt_mps, so a walker it has caught can't step out of its strike and a sprinter can (queue 49 had 3.6, under your walk). leave_mps: sliding away from a room or stretch you lit round it. strike (queue 57's block, CreatureStrike): it rears back (wind-up) when you are within reach_m; strike_m is the same reach. torch_delay (rule.torch_in_hand delay, 'your torch is a delay'): with your torch lit it holds hang_m from you, at the edge of the torch's bright circle, reared and hissing, for hang_s in all before it closes; once it has struck it doesn't hold again until it has given you up; torch out, it closes straight in. feels_m: closer than this it knows you are there whatever your light (so a narrow corridor can't hide you). gives_up (queue 56's block, Pursuit): when it gives you up and goes back to its rounds. watch_s: how long it waits at the edge of its dark while you stand in a lit room before it gives you up. body (BossBody): length_m nose to tail, girth_m thick, head_m the head's length; spacing_m between its body sprites (they overlap two or three deep); coil_r_m the coil's outer radius; undulate_m and wave_m the slither's side-to-side swing and its wavelength; px_head and px_seg the sprites' frame heights in pixels (the bake). torch_delay.sound (queue 57, §FA.2): its hiss while it holds off at your flame, a low, slow, rasping warning (SoundSynth snake_warn), never its strike's sharp hiss (strike.sound, snake_hiss), so the sharp hiss always means the strike is coming; with the head drawing back and the jaws opening, that is its strike's tell. Claude Code's first guesses on Mike's note of 7 Oct: stun_s: a fire pot's burst on or by it stuns it this long (it reels and lies dazed: no strike, no chase), then it flees to its lair hole and down it for fire_pots.json vs_boss.drives_off_s ('a pot cant kill a boss but will stun it/cause it to retreat to its cave temporarily'). flee_mps: how fast it goes fleeing to its hole (after the pot, and the last light's release). peek_m: hunting you, it stops at the edge of the light (residents.json rules.chase_light_cap) and rears its head this far forward into the glow ('they may show just enough of their face/body near the fire'). tunnels: its own (Mike: 'they may have their own tunnels- this can be the case for the snake'), see tunnels._help.

tunnels._help: Claude Code's first guesses on Mike's note of 7 Oct ('depending on the ruins boss type as well, they may have their own tunnels- this can be the case for the snake. it wont actually despawn and respawn places, it needa to physically maneuvar around the ruins to make it anywheres'). BossGround.place_tunnels, TombBuild (the holes), Boss (the way through). holes: [least, most] a tomb, its own dice: one in its lair room, then one in each other side way, then any side room or corridor, apart_m apart; none in the hearth room, on the spine or the way out, nor on a stair. Each is a round-topped hole w_m wide and h_m high at the foot of a wall, cut depth_m into the wall's fitted stone like the niches, a few stones and scratches round it, the style's stone, dark inside; clear of its wall's doors (their frames and door_clear_m), corners (corner_clear_m), torches, airways, a catacomb's niches and a crypt's coffins (only their end walls), an ossuary's bone piles, a fallen room's slab, the pillars and the lair's hole. You can't fit: the wall's collision is whole across it. The holes are joined by tunnels under the floors (under_m beneath the lowest floor on the way), each hole to its nearest and every one to the lair room's; the snake goes in head first, its whole body following, travels hidden at its speed (so a tunnel takes its length over the speed, always longer than the straight line between its holes), and comes out of the other hole. Its ground counts the tunnels as ways (BossGround), so it goes under a lit stretch between it and the dark or its lair, and on its rounds now and then from one side way to another. out_m: the floor before a hole, where it comes out. While it is inside, its tell is muffled: muffle_db quieter, and nothing over muffle_hz.
